questions.stem: State the conversion that platelet chemicals trigger in the plasma.
questions.modelAnswer: Soluble fibrinogen is converted into insoluble fibrin.

questions.stem: Name the final protective layer that forms over a healed-over wound.
questions.modelAnswer: The dried clot develops into a scab over the wound.

questions.stem: Explain why the insolubility of fibrin matters for the clot.
questions.modelAnswer: Because a soluble protein would wash away with the blood; insoluble fibrin stays put, weaving a stable mesh that holds the clot in place.

questions.stem: A person with very few platelets bruises easily and bleeds long after small cuts. Explain the link.
questions.modelAnswer: With too few platelets, the fibrin cascade barely starts, so the mesh forms slowly or not at all, and unclotted blood keeps escaping while germs can enter.
